headline.caveat: BlackRock-led bond raise for the venture, priced Jul 27, 2026 at a 7.53% yield (~287.5bp over 10yr Treasuries)

realized_to_date.caveat: notes priced/sold Jul 27, 2026; proceeds fund construction through 2028

nature_md: BlackRock — whose Global Infrastructure Partners and HPS Investment Partners funds hold the 80% equity stake in the El Paso venture (Project Sopaipilla Holdings) alongside Meta's 20% — led and structured a $12.5B bond sale for the SPV, priced July 27, 2026 at 7.53%, the widest spread for an A-or-better-rated bond in roughly three years. Ultimate noteholders are dispersed institutional buyers in the BlackRock-led offering; this edge records BlackRock as sponsor/arranger and equity principal of the debt-issuing vehicle. Pricing at 7.53% vs Hyperion's 6.58% nine months earlier is a widely cited marker of AI-infrastructure credit repricing.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: GIP/HPS funds hold the 80% equity position (client capital, fee-earning AUM); the $12.5B of notes were distributed to third-party institutional investors in a BlackRock-led offering — BlackRock Inc.'s own balance-sheet exposure is limited.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Debt of the SPV, serviced by Meta's lease payments as sole occupant of the 1GW campus (completion expected 2028). Off Meta's balance sheet; Meta holds only its 20% equity-method stake.

both_sides_md: **Bear:** 7.53% for A-rated, Meta-leased collateral means lenders are demanding nearly 300bp over Treasuries for single-tenant AI risk — the credit market's clearest 2026 signal that it prices these structures as riskier than the ratings imply. **Bull:** the deal cleared at $12.5B — demand exists at the right price, and hedging a 1GW campus with third-party capital at a fixed spread is rational for Meta even at a visibly higher coupon than Hyperion (Bloomberg, Forbes coverage).

observations.metric_label: Yield on El Paso SPV notes
observations.notes: ~95bp wider than the Hyperion JV's 6.58% notes of Oct 2025.
